label: Q-02
title: recipient is guarded against address(0) but not against address(this): an annihilation can come to rest ON the contract
fingerprintNote: sha256(contract:function:rootCauseClass)[:16] - legacy form, empty entryPoint. Carried verbatim from sanitized.json; reproduces from fingerprintBasis.
sources: faithfulness-findings.json note 1 (same observation, Law-3/known-invalid suppressed there)

classification.assetImpact: Self-inflicted: the full ~2x payout comes to rest ON Antimatter with the antimatter already burned. Recoverable by the owner via rescueERC20.
attackPath: 2. :236 mints to Antimatter and :237 transfers from Antimatter to itself.
3. The payout is stranded on the contract.
classification.likelihood: Low - caller error only, no attacker gain.

justification: QA. The C4 'user input mistake' class partially applies and is what holds this at QA rather than higher - correctly, since there is no attacker gain and rescueERC20 recovers it. Not suppressed outright, because the contract already guards address(0) at :203 and its own stated settle-whole-or-not-at-all design implies this case; address(this) is exactly as cheap to reject as address(0).
recommendation: Add `if (recipient == address(this)) revert ...;` alongside the existing zero check - address(this) is exactly as cheap to reject as address(0).

sanitizer.reason: No known-issues document exists for this project (knownIssuesFile/Source null, knownIssues empty, verified at HEAD) so KI suppression has no authority; no C4 known-invalid class genuinely applies; not a malicious-owner vector; ledger empty so no prior entry to reconcile against.

additionalContext.rootCause: Passing address(this) is accepted: :236 mints `amount` phUSD to Antimatter and :237 transfers mintedForStable from Antimatter to itself, so the full ~2x payout comes to rest on the contract with the antimatter already burned.
additionalContext.mitigatingFacts: The phUSD is recoverable by the owner via rescueERC20 (:263), and a later annihilation's phUSDBefore snapshot at :220 correctly excludes it so it is not swept to the next annihilator (control-tested). No partial settlement is created.

mergeAction: CODE-008 kept as the framing; the faithfulness note is the same observation reaching a suppress verdict and is merged as a source rather than left as a divergent record. Resolution: filed at QA, not suppressed - it is a one-line guard the contract's own stated design ('nothing should ever accumulate here', :261-262) asks for, even though the C4 'user input mistake' class is why it does not rise above QA.
